metadata.title: THE RESILIENCE OF STUDENTS WITH AN IMMIGRANT BACKGROUND: AN UPDATE WITH PISA 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper uses PISA 2018 microdata to compare academic, socio-emotional, and motivational resilience outcomes across student groups and OECD countries. Because the paper is a large-scale assessment analysis rather than an ML prediction study, the appropriate approach is to use PISA’s complex survey design features (stratification, clustering, and sampling weights) when estimating population-representative statistics and country comparisons. The manuscript excerpt provided does not specify the exact PISA weight variable name(s) or whether replicate weights were used, so analysts should consult the full PISA 2018 technical documentation and the OECD report’s methods section for the precise weight and variance-estimation procedure. Plausible values are typically used for PISA cognitive achievement domains; for non-cognitive constructs, the report should rely on the corresponding IRT/scale scores as defined by PISA.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD working paper updates the 2018 OECD Strength through Diversity report by analyzing academic, socio-emotional, and motivational resilience among students with an immigrant background using PISA 2018 data across OECD countries. The paper focuses on how outcomes differ across student groups (e.g., first-generation immigrant students and other immigrant-background categories) and how these outcomes have changed in recent years. It also examines key integration barriers and protective factors, including language-related barriers, socio-economic disadvantage, and aspects of well-being such as sense of belonging, life satisfaction, and fear of failure, alongside educational and career expectations. The excerpt does not provide the specific statistical/ML modeling approach, performance metrics, or the exact PV and missing-data procedures, so methodological details must be taken from the full methods section of the report. Policy interpretation is therefore centered on identifying which resilience-related domains appear most strongly associated with integration outcomes, rather than on causal claims.
